result: tDCS induces heterogeneous, polarity-dependent modulation of Purkinje cell (PC) firing rates in awake mice, with some PCs increasing firing during anodal and decreasing during cathodal stimulation, while others show the opposite pattern. This heterogeneity was observed in 11 out of 24 PCs recorded in Crus I/II, with a linear correlation (R=0.46, p=0.0003) between anodal and cathodal effects.
evaluation: All reviewers explicitly affirm this finding as a core result. Reviewer 1 states the study finds 'heterogeneous responses depending on the orientation of the recorded Purkinje cell,' and Reviewer 2 notes the authors 'find a relationship between neuron orientation and firing rate, dependent on stimulation type.' No concerns are raised about the heterogeneous modulation of PC firing rates.

result: Non-Purkinje cells (non-PCs) in Crus I/II also show heterogeneous, polarity-dependent modulation during tDCS, with 35 out of 50 cells showing significant differences (R=0.56, p<0.0001). The non-PC data distribution showed higher dispersion than PC data.
evaluation: Reviewer 2 explicitly notes that 'there is a similar pattern of modulation in Purkinje cells and non-Purkinje cells (excitatory and inhibitory interneurons)' and praises this as providing 'wholistic insight into how tDCS can affect activity across different populations of cells.' No reviewer challenges these findings.

result: In the vermis of anesthetized mice, tDCS shows stronger and more consistent polarity-dependent modulation of PCs compared to Crus I/II. In vermis, 27 out of 31 PCs showed significant modulation with strong linear correlation (R=0.7, p<0.0001), and mean modulation was 62.35% in vermis versus 9.42% in Crus I/II (p<0.001).
evaluation: Reviewer 2 explicitly highlights 'systematic investigation into the effects of tDCS on neural activity across multiple regions of the cerebellum' as a strength, noting 'the pattern of modulation is dependent on the target region.' The regional differences are accepted without challenge by all reviewers.

result: The heterogeneous effects of tDCS on PC firing can be explained by the somatodendritic orientation relative to the electric field. Juxtacellular recordings with anatomical reconstruction showed that PCs with dendrites pointing toward the electrode (θ≈0°) increased firing during anodal and decreased during cathodal tDCS, while PCs with opposite orientation (θ≈180°) showed opposite modulation. PCs perpendicular to the field (θ≈90° or 270°) showed minimal modulation.
evaluation: This is the central finding that all reviewers explicitly affirm. The editor states the study finds 'heterogeneous responses depending on the orientation of the recorded Purkinje cell,' and Reviewer 2 notes the authors 'find a relationship between neuron orientation and firing rate.' Reviewer 1 calls it 'elegant and thorough' and states it 'may well explain part of the controversial and ambiguous outcomes of various clinical trials.'

result: Neuropixels recordings in awake mice simultaneously recorded multiple PCs and confirmed that a single tDCS polarity can modulate individual PCs in opposite directions at the same time, with the direction determined by somatodendritic orientation. PCs with dendrites pointing toward the electrode increased firing during anodal tDCS, while those with opposite orientation decreased firing.
evaluation: Reviewer 2 explicitly praises 'the in vivo nature of this study' and notes 'being able to simultaneously record neural activity and apply exogenous electrical current to the brain during both an anesthetized state and during wakefulness' as a major strength. The simultaneous recording finding is accepted without challenge.

result: Electric field measurements show that field magnitude decreases logarithmically with depth (R=0.98, 0.96, 0.95 for different intensities), with values ranging from 60.1-125.7 V/m at 0.3 mm depth to 5.9-34.6 V/m at 2.3 mm depth for 100-300 μA stimulation intensities.
evaluation: Reviewer 2 notes the study provides 'thorough background, rationale, and interpretation regarding the expected and observed influence of neuronal orientation on excitability modulation by electrical stimulation.' The electric field measurements are not questioned by any reviewer and are treated as methodologically sound supporting data.

result: tDCS had minimal and inconsistent effects on complex spike (CS) firing rate and CS-driven simple spike silence in most PCs. No differences were observed in spike waveforms during tDCS.
evaluation: No reviewer challenges these negative findings. The lack of CS modulation is presented as part of the comprehensive characterization of tDCS effects and is implicitly accepted through the absence of critique.

result: A significant rebound effect was observed after tDCS termination in some neurons, where firing rates changed in the opposite direction after stimulation ended. Firing rate modulation tracked transcranial current dynamics during ramp-in and ramp-out periods.
evaluation: Reviewer 2 notes the authors 'show effects of stimulation intensity and rebound effects' as part of the findings. This observation is accepted without challenge by all reviewers.

result: The study concludes that tDCS-driven firing rate modulation of individual PCs can be predicted by the orientation of the PC's dendrites relative to the electric field, regardless of how tDCS impacts pre-synaptic inputs.
evaluation: This conclusion is directly supported by the reviewers' acceptance of the orientation-dependence findings. Reviewer 1 states the main conclusions are 'correct' after additional statistics, and the editor calls the study 'important and compelling.'

result: Clear firing rate modulation was observed even at low electric field strengths (5.9 V/m at 2.3 mm depth with 100 μA stimulation), demonstrating that tDCS can modulate neuronal activity at relatively weak field intensities.
evaluation: This finding is not challenged by any reviewer. Reviewer 2's comment that the work is 'methodologically sound' implicitly accepts the validity of observations across the range of stimulation parameters tested.
